observations.text: SP executed the closed pattern at the level expected for this training unit, with the IP directing the request for clearance, the point of initiation and the roll out on downwind. MAX power was set only after the IP's command and the bank of the climbing turn varied from the value prescribed by the Techniques and Procedures Manual, so that the level off altitude published in the LAP was regained with the IP flying part of the level off, deviations reaching 450 feet. Downwind was entered at 130 KIAS, below the 140 KIAS minimum, and the spacing against existing traffic was assessed from the rear cockpit. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent initiation of the maneuver and unassisted control of bank and airspeed are expected to develop in the following sorties.

SP flew the closed pattern using only the IP's verbal indications, without any IP input on the stick or the throttle. MAX power was set after prompting, the climbing turn was flown with the bank prescribed by the Techniques and Procedures Manual and the onset of stall characteristics was not allowed at any point. The deviation from the level off altitude published in the LAP reached 300 feet and downwind was entered at 138 KIAS, both recognized and corrected with delay after the IP's call. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP requested the closed pattern from ATC and initiated the maneuver without IP's intervention, setting MAX power at the initiation and adjusting power afterwards as required. Minor errors in the rate of the climbing turn produced a deviation of 200 feet from the level off altitude published in the LAP, recognized and corrected by SP in a timely manner. Downwind was entered at 145 KIAS according to existing traffic and no stall characteristics were allowed to develop. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the closed pattern with accuracy and speed, following the standard procedure of the Techniques and Procedures Manual and the LAP after the ATC clearance. MAX power was set initially and adjusted afterwards as required, and the bank and the airspeeds of the climbing turn were held within the values prescribed by the Flight Manual. The level off altitude published in the LAP was held within 100 feet, downwind was entered at 150 KIAS according to existing traffic and no IP intervention was required. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP initiated the closed pattern immediately on receipt of the ATC clearance and flew the whole maneuver with exceptional precision. MAX power was set at the initiation and reduced at the exact point required, the bank of the climbing turn was held constant at the value prescribed by the Techniques and Procedures Manual and the onset of stall characteristics was never approached. The deviation from the level off altitude published in the LAP remained negligible at 40 feet, downwind was entered at 152 KIAS and the spacing against the A/C already established in the pattern needed no adjustment. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a power technique that left the PCL short of MAX power at the initiation of the closed pattern, could not complete the climbing turn without assistance and did not maintain the airspeeds prescribed by the Flight Manual and the Techniques and Procedures Manual. Airspeed decayed to 118 KIAS with the onset of stall characteristics allowed to develop in the turn, and the A/C rolled out 500 feet below the level off altitude published in the LAP, with the result that the IP took the controls and re-established the A/C in the pattern. Repetition of the power, bank and airspeed sequence of the closed pattern on the ground trainer is required.

SP, due to loss of situational awareness of the A/C's position in the pattern after the go around, did not initiate the closed pattern at the point prescribed by the LAP and did not enter downwind according to existing traffic. The climbing turn was continued past the downwind heading and the A/C passed 450 feet above the level off altitude published in the LAP, with the result that the IP directed the roll out and flew part of the return to the published altitude. The position of the A/C already established on downwind was not taken into account until it was called from the rear cockpit.

SP executed the closed pattern at the level expected for this training unit, initiating the maneuver and flying the climbing turn after verbal prompts from the IP and without any IP input on the controls. MAX power was set late, so that the deviation from the level off altitude published in the LAP reached 300 feet and downwind was entered at 136 KIAS, both recognized and corrected with delay. Marginal performance for the Training Section - unprompted initiation of the maneuver and timely correction of the level off altitude are expected to improve in the following sorties.

SP initiated the closed pattern after the ATC clearance without prompting from the rear cockpit and set MAX power at the initiation. The rate of the climbing turn was allowed to reduce and the A/C leveled 200 feet below the level off altitude published in the LAP, and SP recognized the deviation and regained the published altitude in a timely manner and without IP's intervention. Downwind was entered at 148 KIAS according to existing traffic and the onset of stall characteristics was not allowed. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the closed pattern accurately and quickly, following the standard procedure of the Techniques and Procedures Manual and the LAP after the takeoff. MAX power was set initially and adjusted afterwards as required, and the bank and the airspeeds of the climbing turn were maintained within the values prescribed by the Flight Manual. The level off altitude published in the LAP was held within 110 feet, downwind was entered at 149 KIAS according to existing traffic and no IP intervention was required at any point. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the closed pattern with exceptional precision on each repetition of the sortie, initiating the maneuver immediately on receipt of the ATC clearance. Bank was held constant at the value prescribed by the Techniques and Procedures Manual, MAX power was set at the initiation and adjusted at the exact point required, and the onset of stall characteristics was never approached. Deviations from the level off altitude published in the LAP remained negligible at 50 feet, downwind was entered at 155 KIAS and the spacing against the traffic already established required no correction. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a closed pattern initiated before the minimum airspeed of 140 KIAS had been reached, could not complete the climbing turn without assistance and did not maintain the airspeeds prescribed by the Flight Manual and the Techniques and Procedures Manual. Airspeed decayed to 115 KIAS at the bank prescribed for the maneuver, the onset of stall characteristics was allowed to develop and the A/C remained 500 feet below the level off altitude published in the LAP, with the result that the IP took the controls and unloaded the A/C. The airspeed gate for the initiation of the closed pattern is to be reworked before the next sortie.

SP, due to task sequencing that concentrated the R/T request, the power setting and the roll in inside the climbing turn, did not follow the standard procedure of the Techniques and Procedures Manual and did not monitor the level off altitude published in the LAP. The A/C passed 400 feet above the published altitude with the bank held beyond the value prescribed for the maneuver, with the result that the IP directed the roll out and flew part of the return to pattern altitude. Downwind was entered without reference to the A/C already established in the pattern, and the sequence was re-established only after the IP's direction.

SP, due to a climbing turn flown with the bank progressively reduced after the initiation, did not follow the standard procedure of the Techniques and Procedures Manual and did not roll out on the downwind heading at the point prescribed by the LAP. The deviation from the level off altitude published in the LAP reached 300 feet and downwind was entered at 134 KIAS, corrected by SP with delay after the IP's verbal prompts and without intervention on the controls. Maintenance of a constant bank through the climbing turn is to be reworked.

SP, due to an interrupted cross-check of the A/C state after the gear and flap retraction, did not monitor airspeed and altitude through the climbing turn of the closed pattern. Airspeed decayed to 132 KIAS, below the 140 KIAS minimum for the downwind entry, and the A/C leveled 300 feet above the level off altitude published in the LAP, both recognized and corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts. No intervention on the controls was required, but the cross-check was re-established after prompting rather than by SP alone.

SP executed the closed pattern within the desired standards, setting MAX power at the initiation, holding the bank prescribed by the Techniques and Procedures Manual and entering downwind at 146 KIAS according to existing traffic. The level off was anticipated late on two of the three repetitions and the A/C passed 220 feet above the level off altitude published in the LAP, recognized and corrected by SP in a timely manner and without IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - anticipation of the level off and consistency between repetitions are expected to improve.

SP executed the closed pattern with accuracy and speed after the ATC clearance, following the standard procedure of the Techniques and Procedures Manual and the LAP on every repetition. MAX power was set initially and adjusted afterwards as required, the bank and the airspeeds of the climbing turn were held within the values prescribed by the Flight Manual and the onset of stall characteristics was not allowed. The level off altitude published in the LAP was held within 90 feet and downwind was entered at 150 KIAS according to existing traffic, without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the closed pattern with exceptional precision after both the takeoff and the go around, initiating the maneuver immediately on receipt of the ATC clearance and above the 140 KIAS minimum. Bank was held constant at the value prescribed by the Techniques and Procedures Manual, MAX power was set at the initiation and reduced at the exact point required, and the onset of stall characteristics was never approached. Deviations from the level off altitude published in the LAP remained negligible at 40 feet and the spacing against the A/C already established on downwind was planned in advance and needed no adjustment. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a pitch attitude in the climbing turn that was not adjusted when MAX power was set, could not fly the closed pattern without assistance and did not maintain the airspeeds prescribed by the Flight Manual and the Techniques and Procedures Manual. Airspeed decayed to 112 KIAS with the onset of stall characteristics allowed to develop in the turn, and the A/C rolled out 550 feet above the level off altitude published in the LAP, with the result that the IP took the controls and re-established the A/C on downwind. The relationship between power, pitch attitude and bank in the closed pattern is to be reworked on the ground trainer.

SP, due to lack of assertiveness in stating "unable" when the closed pattern clearance could not be complied with against the A/C already on downwind, did not enter downwind according to existing traffic and did not follow the standard procedure of the LAP. The climbing turn was tightened and then stopped short of the downwind heading, airspeed decayed to 120 KIAS and the A/C settled 450 feet below the level off altitude published in the LAP, with the result that the IP took the controls and repositioned the A/C in the pattern. The conflict had been recognized by SP but was not voiced on the R/T.

SP, due to a roll in to the closed pattern begun before the wings-level acceleration to the minimum airspeed had been completed, did not maintain the airspeeds prescribed by the Techniques and Procedures Manual through the climbing turn. Downwind was entered at 128 KIAS, below the 140 KIAS minimum, and the deviation from the level off altitude published in the LAP reached 300 feet, both corrected with delay after the IP's verbal prompts. No intervention on the controls was required, but the airspeed gate for the initiation of the maneuver was applied only after prompting.

SP, due to distraction by the R/T exchange with the tower during the climbing turn, did not monitor the level off altitude published in the LAP and did not adjust power after the initial MAX power setting. The A/C passed the published altitude and the deviation reached 300 feet before the correction was started, following the IP's verbal prompts, and downwind was entered at 137 KIAS. Recognition and correction were made with delay, although no IP input on the controls was required.

SP, due to a level off begun without the lead required at the climb rate of the closed pattern, passed 200 feet above the level off altitude published in the LAP on the first repetition of the maneuver. SP recognized the overshoot, reduced power and regained the published altitude in a timely manner and without IP's intervention, and the two following repetitions were leveled within 100 feet. Bank, airspeeds and the standard procedure of the Techniques and Procedures Manual were maintained throughout, and the onset of stall characteristics was not allowed.

SP, due to attention captured by the A/C already established on downwind while the altitude went unmonitored, did not level off at the altitude published in the LAP on completion of the climbing turn. The deviation reached 240 feet before SP recognized it, and the published altitude and the 140 KIAS minimum airspeed were both regained in a timely manner and without IP's intervention. The error was minor and the spacing against the traffic in the pattern was maintained throughout.

SP executed the closed pattern within the desired standards, initiating the maneuver on the ATC clearance, setting MAX power and holding the bank and the airspeeds prescribed by the Techniques and Procedures Manual without IP's intervention. The level off was flown slowly on two repetitions, with the deviation from the level off altitude published in the LAP reaching 140 feet and the downwind entry stabilized later than the LAP profile requires. Marginal performance for the Training Section - speed of the level off is expected to improve while the present accuracy of bank and airspeed control is maintained.

SP flew the closed pattern with exceptional precision on every repetition of the sortie, after the takeoff and after the go around, initiating the maneuver immediately on receipt of the ATC clearance and above the 140 KIAS minimum. MAX power was set at the initiation and adjusted at the exact point required, the bank of the climbing turn was held constant at the value prescribed by the Techniques and Procedures Manual and the onset of stall characteristics was never approached. Deviations from the level off altitude published in the LAP remained negligible at 30 feet, and downwind was entered with the spacing against the established traffic planned in advance and requiring no adjustment. Above end of block MIF achieved.
